spans.text: The non-linear smooth fixed-effect predictors were shortest path length from epicenter (SPE), nodal hazard, baseline atrophy W-score, Euclidean distance to epicenter, and clinical dementia rating baseline score (CDR) interactions with SPE and nodal hazard.

model_settings.value: Generalized additive model fitted with the mgcv package in R; nonlinear smooth fixed effects used spline basis functions with maximum basis dimension k=5 and a penalty minimizing the second derivative. Terms included shortest path length to epicenter, nodal hazard, baseline atrophy, Euclidean distance to epicenter, CDR interactions with shortest path length and nodal hazard, plus linear effects of interscan interval, age, sex, diagnosis, and cortical/subcortical node. The model included subject random intercepts, node-specific random slopes for the baseline atrophy/subsequent atrophy relationship, and a Gaussian-process spatial autocorrelation term with a Matern correlation function, range 167 mm, and k=10. Models were compared using likelihood-ratio tests.
